_: Every setting uibridge has, at its default value. Copy this to
config.json and delete the lines you do not want to change - an omitted
key uses the default shown here, so a short file is the normal case.
Keys beginning with _ are ignored, so you can leave notes. Any OTHER key
this build does not recognise is a startup error, naming the key and the
nearest match: a misspelled setting that changed nothing silently is a
worse outcome than a config that will not load.
Paths are relative to the state directory (`uibridge paths` prints it).
_port: The daemon and the OpenAI-compatible API. Give a second uibridge on the same machine its own port.
_basePort: First Chrome remote-debugging port; each provider takes the next one. Change if something else on this machine uses 9333.
_headless: How the browser is shown, for everything except signing in (that always
opens a real visible window - it is a human action).
"offscreen" a real browser parked off the visible desktop (default)
false       a visible window you can watch
MEASURED: ChatGPT serves an ANONYMOUS session to true headless even with
valid cookies, so its block below pins "offscreen". Gemini is fine
headless. `uibridge serve --headed` overrides for one run.
_profileDir: Chrome profiles, one per provider. Your logins live here. Never commit it.
_ledgerDir: Per-thread JSONL: what was sent, what came back, file hashes.
_requestDir: Durable request records, keyed by Idempotency-Key.
_requestTimeoutMs: Whole-request budget at the API layer, above the per-phase timeouts below.

provider._: Applies to every provider. The per-provider blocks below override it.
provider._concurrency: Tabs driven at once for this provider. Raising it does not raise the site's own limits.
provider._minIntervalMs: Minimum spacing between request STARTS, across all tabs. Fresh conversations are what trips these sites' throttling, and a batch pipeline is exactly the caller that would burst. Set per provider below.
provider._continuationIntervalMs: Spacing for follow-ups in an existing thread. 0 because a continuation creates no new conversation.
provider._newChatPerRequest: A fresh conversation per request: no shared context, and the model choice actually applies (switching mid-thread is unreliable). Pass thread_id to continue instead.
provider._maxComposerChars: Above this the prompt is sent as a temporary UTF-8 attachment instead of typed, because large pastes truncate or stall the editor.
provider._submitAckMs: How long to wait for a turn to appear after sending. Short on purpose: a prompt that never went out should fail in a minute, not sit for the full response budget.
provider._responseTimeoutMs: A thinking model can take minutes. This is the ceiling for one answer.
provider._threadResumeMs: how long a requested thread has to appear in the URL after we navigate to it; nothing is sent until it does
provider._fileWaitMs: Budget for retrieving one generated file once the page has been asked for it.
provider._settleChecks: Consecutive identical reads that mean 'the answer has stopped growing'. A measurement of stability, not padding.
_strictModel: true  a model that could not be verified is an error (502). Use this
when provenance matters more than getting an answer: a review
must not attribute a row to a model that did not write it.
false the request proceeds and is recorded as unverified, which is
provider._errorTextExtra: Extra provider failure wordings, as regex source strings. A provider can change its error text at any time and you will meet the new one before we do; adding it here needs no code change. See core/answer-integrity.mjs.
provider._failOnSuspectedProviderError: Turn a SUSPECTED failure (an answer that opens like an apology but matches no measured pattern) into a 502 instead of a flag. Off by default: a terse refusal can be legitimate content. On for pipelines that would rather lose a row than record a bad one.
provider._errorNoticeMaxChars: Longer text that merely contains an apology is an answer, not a failure notice.

providers._: Per provider. Anything from `provider` above is valid here too, plus url and debugPort.

gemini._settleChecks: Gemini streams in bursts with visible pauses; fewer checks ends a read inside one of them.
gemini._url: The site address. Defaults to the measured one in the provider's selectors.json - only set it for a regional domain or a local stand-in, and expect selectors to need re-measuring.

chatgpt._headless: MEASURED: true headless gets an anonymous session here even with valid cookies.
chatgpt._minIntervalMs: ChatGPT locks access to your conversations after a burst of new chats. Twenty seconds is what kept this account out of that lock.
